I've been farming this land for 20 years. I know what works and what doesn't. My husband helps when he can, and my older children do too, so I have enough hands for cotton, which is tiring work. We need the income from all three crops to feed seven people and cover school fees.

**My thinking:**

My 10.1 mu is split — about 7 mu in wheat-maize rotation, and 3.1 mu I keep for cotton on a separate plot. Cotton prices have been uncertain lately but I still grow it because the payment comes in autumn when we need cash. Wheat and maize I grow mostly for the household and to sell the surplus.

For wheat, I plant in October after the maize is in. I use the improved variety the village seed shop sells — same one I've used for several years, it did well. I apply base fertilizer before planting and top-dress at jointing. I irrigate three times: before sowing to wet the soil, at jointing, and at heading. I spray twice — once for aphids in spring, once for powdery mildew if it shows up.

For maize, I plant straight after wheat harvest in June. I always use hybrid seed — it yields much more. I don't plough again, just rotary till lightly to break the stubble and plant. I top-dress urea at the V6 stage and again at silking. I only irrigate if it's very dry — summer rains usually help.

For cotton, I plough the plot in early spring, transplant seedlings in late April. Cotton needs the most work — I spray many times for bollworm and aphids, though Bt cotton helps a lot with bollworm. I water more frequently because cotton doesn't like drought during boll setting.

I keep my inputs similar to last year. I don't change too much at once — if something goes wrong I need to know what caused it.
